takeaway: The breast's arterial supply comes mainly from the internal thoracic (internal mammary) artery, with contributions from intercostal and axillary branches.

lines.text: A 49-year-old woman has a unilateral mastectomy for carcinoma of the breast.
lines.say: A forty-nine-year-old woman has a unilateral mastectomy for carcinoma of the breast.

lines.text: One breast has been removed. That is what unilateral means.
So which artery supplies most of the blood to the female breast?
The main supply comes from the internal thoracic artery,
also called the internal mammary artery.
Its branches are the primary contributor to the breast's arterial supply.
Intercostal and axillary branches add smaller contributions to the supply.
